title: Vagaja2023: Motor-imagery EEG during embodiment-primed MI-BCI training in VR
description: EEG recordings from 26 healthy volunteers performing cued left- versus right-hand motor imagery during a single MI-BCI training run in immersive virtual reality. Participants were randomized to an embodiment-primed group (virtual hand illusion) or a non-embodied control group. The recordings include 32-channel EEG, bipolar EMG, skin temperature and accelerometry, and are re-released in BIDS format via MOABB.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 500 Hz with a Brain Products LiveAmp 32 and actiCAP active Ag/AgCl electrodes (32 EEG channels, 2 EMG, 4 misc) using BrainVision Recorder. Each participant completed one lab session with 40 cue-based trials (20 per class), each with a 10 s imagery/feedback window, with visual feedback in VR.
